core_obligations: Observe that under Gal(M/K) -> Gal(L/K) the groups P', I', D' map into P, I, D, immediately from the definitions of these groups (proof lines 33660-33662).

Establish commutativity of the first diagram, noting that since kappa(m)/kappa_A is normal every automorphism of kappa(m') over kappa_A induces one of kappa(m) over kappa_A, which is what produces the right vertical arrow (proof lines 33662-33668).
Show that I' -> I and D' -> D are surjective using the one-orbit geometric Galois comparison lemma (proof lines 33671-33672).
Conclude that P' -> P is surjective because P' and P are Sylow p-subgroups of I' and I respectively (proof lines 33673-33674).
To prove commutativity of the second diagram, choose uniformizers pi' of C_{m'} and pi of B_m, and write pi = c' (pi')^{e'/e} for some unit c' (proof lines 33677-33679).

For sigma' in I' with image sigma in I, write sigma'(pi') = c pi' and sigma(pi) = b pi with c and b units, and compute b pi = sigma'(pi) = sigma'(c') c^{e'/e} (pi')^{e'/e} = (sigma'(c')/c') c^{e'/e} pi, which identifies the two maps into the roots of unity up to the power e'/e (proof lines 33680-33688 and following).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K, a tower M/L/K with both extensions finite Galois, the integral closures C and B of A in M and L, a maximal ideal m' of C with m = m' cap B, and the chains of wild inertia, inertia and decomposition groups of m and m'; it asserts that the canonical surjection Gal(M/K) -> Gal(L/K) restricts to surjections P' -> P, I' -> I and D' -> D, and that these fit into two commutative diagrams, the second involving the ramification indices e' and e and the maps theta', theta into the groups of roots of unity of the residue fields (source lines 33619-33657). The first part is immediate from the definitions: the groups map into one another, and commutativity of the first diagram is clear because the residue extension kappa(m)/kappa_A is normal, so every automorphism of kappa(m') over kappa_A induces one of kappa(m) over kappa_A (proof lines 33660-33668). Surjectivity of I' -> I and D' -> D comes from the one-orbit geometric lemma, and surjectivity of P' -> P then follows because P' and P are Sylow p-subgroups of I' and I (proof lines 33671-33674). The substantive part is the commutativity of the second diagram: with uniformizers pi' of C_{m'} and pi of B_m one has pi = c' (pi')^{e'/e} for a unit c', and for sigma' in I' with image sigma in I, writing sigma'(pi') = c pi' and sigma(pi) = b pi, the proof computes b pi = sigma'(pi) = sigma'(c') c^{e'/e} (pi')^{e'/e} = (sigma'(c')/c') c^{e'/e} pi, so that this is sheer algebra with the ramification indices (proof lines 33677-33688 and following). The non-routine content is the uniformizer computation that identifies the two maps into the roots of unity up to the power e'/e.
